title: Stairway to the stars
caption: Reaching for Jupiter beneath the Milky Way, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Standing at the head of a staircase, ESO Photo Ambassador Petr Horálek reaches up toward what looks like a single very bright star among many. It is actually the planet Jupiter, shining in front of thousands of stars that belong to the Milky Way.

The Milky Way arcs across this panorama and leads the eye down to the four Unit Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope. Our galaxy contains billions of stars, and the ones visible here are only a tiny share of them.

At the far left of the photograph are the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds, the Milky Way's two satellite galaxies. The scene layers distances in one frame, from a nearby planet within our Solar System to stars inside our galaxy and two separate galaxies beyond it, all appearing side by side from where the photographer stands.

understand.summary: This is a panoramic landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: Jupiter is easy to see with the naked eye, but a long exposure reveals far more stars and makes the Milky Way and Magellanic Clouds brighter than they would appear in person.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Planets such as Jupiter can outshine most stars in the night sky, which is why they are easily mistaken for unusually bright stars. The playful pose makes use of that.
alt: A person at the top of a staircase reaching toward a bright point of light, with the Milky Way arcing over four large telescopes and two hazy galaxies at far left.
